data.narrative:
Inari, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company founded by David Berry, Ignacio Martinez, and John Casey, is evaluated against a comp universe of nine private peers and one public comparator (277810.KQ). The company has raised $874.1M to date across all rounds.

Two valuation methods triangulate to a defensible range. The stage-progression method, applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement, implies $1.5B valuation from the $874M capital raised proxy. The peer-median method benchmarks Inari against seven same-sector, same/adjacent-stage peers—including Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), and Hadrian ($1.6B, Series D)—yielding a median valuation of $1.6B with a range of $1.0B to $2.0B.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $1.3B (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $1.6B. This range reflects convergence between stage-based progression and peer multiples, though key uncertainties remain: the extent of revenue traction within the peer set is not specified, capital efficiency metrics are unavailable, and stage heterogeneity within the peer cohort (Series B through Series D) introduces some dispersion. The $300M band between low and high estimates captures reasonable variance in comparable company multiples and stage-specific deployment dynamics.
